I built my brother a PC for about $750 four years ago, he only now had to put the first upgraded parts in to it about a month ago. (new motherboard, processor, and RAM - he was seriously CPU-bound on his old build in terms of framerate)

Off the top of my head, the kind of major parts I would recommend right now for an affordable build:

Quad-core processor

16GB DDR3 RAM (DDR4 would work better, but it's also more expensive - the important bit is the 16GB)

750+ watt Power supply

nVidia GTX 880 or greater OR AMD R9 290 or greater - I've personally had better luck with nVidia cards, but either of these will run most games at decent or better settings

2TB 7200 RPM or faster HDD (hard drive) with a separate smaller drive (HDD or SSD) for the OS - it's important that you have your games on whichever drive doesn't have the OS because then things will load faster, but I wouldn't recommend getting an SSD for your games (yet) because they're still too small to fit many games on them; you'd have to constantly swap out which games are on the SSD depending on what you wanted to load quickly

I'd speak of my own PCs, but I'm nowhere near that conservative when spending on myself - my latest build has been about $1900 (I have a job, whereas my brother is still in school).
